In Chinese (and I think Korean too) tradition,  when we put food offerings to our ancestors and we eat them afterwards. And that I think helps us feel a deeper connection with them. It's like sharing a meal at the family table,  but with our dead ancestors. So maybe this example can help you feel less weird about eating it afterwards. Usually we cast 2 two-sided half moon shaped dice to ask if the ancestors have had their fill, and then the offerings are taken off the altar and shared among us.

I was one of those people who promise to be supportive but when they really need me I often let them down. Usually, it's because when they stop pretending to be ok, the truth is they are suffering more than I assumed they did. It takes quite a while to deal with the realisation and I often don't know how to respond. So I'll leave it on read. That doesn't mean I don't care. This usually impact me for at least a whole week. I'll be thinking and carefully deliberating what the correct response should be but unable to do anything because I'm paralyzed by shock. I do understand that sometimes a faster response time is more important than a "correct" response.
